summary: The stylesheet for the whole app. It sets the dark theme, buttons, the upload and project chooser pages, the 3D viewer panels, and layouts for narrower screens.
purpose: Controls how every screen looks: colours, fonts, spacing, panel layouts and the changes made for small screens.
why: Likely reason: one stylesheet keeps the look consistent. The file is grouped by screen, with shared rules first and page-specific rules after.
how: The file starts with theme colour variables and base element rules, then shared buttons, then each page in order: upload, chooser, mapping, viewer panels, timeline, and the programme view. The media query blocks near the end adjust layouts for narrower screens.
inputs: Class names and element types that the app's screens set, such as buttons, panels, inputs and status dots.
outputs: Visual styling in the browser. It produces no data.
risks: Some selectors appear more than once, such as control-label, phase-list, phase-pill, inspector and programme-grid, so a later rule can override an earlier one. Some selector lists continue across section boundaries, so the outline can mislead when searching.
debug: In the browser's element inspector, select the element to see which rule applies and where it is written. If a layout breaks on small screens, check the media query blocks near the end. If colours look wrong, check the variables at the top.
